title: Why Puiseux's Theorem Fails in Characteristic p: the Artin–Schreier Obstruction
description: Addresses the parent's open question on the positive-characteristic analogue of Puiseux's theorem by formalizing the precise obstruction in the negative direction. The Artin–Schreier equation yᵖ − y = x⁻¹ over 𝔽_p((x)) has a Hahn-series root with exponents {−1/pᵏ} of unbounded ramification: no fixed denominator clears all the pᵏ. We prove these exponents are distinct (strictly monotone), that the set lies in no (1/n)·ℤ, and hence that any Hahn series carrying them is NOT a Puiseux series — the exact reason classical Puiseux fails in characteristic p. The positive analogue (Kedlaya's automatic series via Artin–Schreier–Witt theory) remains the open follow-up.

meta.author: Lean Genius
meta.assumptions: No axioms (#print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). The theorem artinSchreier_support_not_puiseux is stated for ANY Hahn series whose support contains the Artin–Schreier exponents {−1/pᵏ}; the existence of such a series — the Artin–Schreier root of yᵖ − y = x⁻¹, a separable degree-p algebraic element over the Laurent series — is the classical input, documented but not constructed here (its construction needs the well-ordering of the support and a Frobenius computation in characteristic p). The IsPuiseuxSeries predicate is reproduced verbatim from the gallery puiseux-theorem entry, whose own source is a work-in-progress that does not compile against current Mathlib, so this file is kept self-contained.

overview.historicalContext: Puiseux's theorem (Victor Puiseux, 1850; algorithm due to Newton, 1676) says that over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 the fractional power series — Puiseux series, with bounded ramification — form the algebraic closure of the Laurent series, so every algebraic function has a fractional-power-series expansion. The theorem is FALSE in positive characteristic, and the reason is wild ramification. The cleanest witness is the Artin–Schreier equation yᵖ − y = x⁻¹: separable of degree p over 𝔽_p((x)), its Hahn-series solution y = ∑_{k≥1} x^{−1/pᵏ} satisfies yᵖ = x⁻¹ + y by the Frobenius/Freshman's-dream identity, yet its exponents involve every denominator pᵏ, so no single ramification index n suffices and y is not a Puiseux series. The correct positive-characteristic analogue — describing the actual algebraic closure of 𝔽_p((x)) inside the Hahn series — was settled much later by Kedlaya (2001, 'The algebraic closure of the power series field in positive characteristic') using Artin–Schreier–Witt theory and the notion of 'automatic'/'additive' series. This entry formalizes the obstruction (the negative direction): the precise sense in which the classical statement must fail.
overview.problemStatement:
**OQ-01 of puiseux-theorem**

What is the correct analogue of Puiseux's theorem in positive characteristic? (Requires Artin–Schreier–Witt theory.)

This entry isolates and verifies the obstruction: classical Puiseux series cannot be algebraically closed in characteristic p, because the Artin–Schreier root has unbounded ramification.
overview.text: The Artin–Schreier exponent set {−1/p^{k+1}} has unbounded ramification, so any Hahn series carrying it (the Artin–Schreier root of yᵖ − y = x⁻¹) is algebraic over the Laurent series yet not Puiseux.
overview.proofStrategy:
**The unbounded-ramification obstruction.**
1. Define artinSchreierExp p k = −1/p^{k+1}, the exponents of the Artin–Schreier root.
2. Show they are strictly monotone (hence distinct): x ↦ 1/x is antitone, p^{k+1} is strictly increasing.
3. Core (artinSchreierExp_denominators_unbounded): suppose all exponents lay in (1/n)·ℤ. Pick k with p^{k+1} > n (powers of p are unbounded). Then −1/p^{k+1} = j/n clears to n = −j·p^{k+1}, so p^{k+1} ∣ n in ℤ, forcing p^{k+1} ≤ n — contradiction.
4. Conclude (artinSchreier_support_not_puiseux): any Hahn series whose support contains these exponents fails IsPuiseuxSeries. The Artin–Schreier root has exactly this support, witnessing the failure of Puiseux's theorem in characteristic p.
keyInsights: The entire failure of Puiseux's theorem in characteristic p is captured by one arithmetic fact: the denominators pᵏ of the Artin–Schreier root's exponents are unbounded, so no single ramification index works. This is wild ramification made completely elementary.

Bounded ramification (the IsPuiseuxSeries condition: support ⊆ (1/n)·ℤ for a FIXED n) is exactly what Artin–Schreier extensions destroy — each iterated extension multiplies the ramification by another factor of p.

The obstruction is stated about ANY Hahn series carrying the exponents, decoupling the elementary arithmetic from the (harder) construction of the Artin–Schreier root itself. The root's existence is the classical input; the non-Puiseux conclusion is the verified content.

Honesty boundary: this is the NEGATIVE half of the open question (classical Puiseux must fail). The POSITIVE analogue — Kedlaya's identification of the algebraic closure of 𝔽_p((x)) as the 'automatic' Hahn series via Artin–Schreier–Witt theory — is deep and not formalized here; it is recorded as the open follow-up.

Frobenius / Freshman's dream (a+b)ᵖ = aᵖ + bᵖ in characteristic p is what makes y = ∑ x^{−1/pᵏ} solve yᵖ − y = x⁻¹: raising to the p-th power shifts every exponent −1/pᵏ to −1/p^{k−1}, reproducing the series plus the x⁻¹ term.
prerequisites: The gallery puiseux-theorem entry and its IsPuiseuxSeries predicate (bounded denominators)
Elementary divisibility in ℤ and unboundedness of pᵏ

sections.title: Module Header and Background
sections.summary: Extensive docstring: states classical Puiseux (bounded ramification, char 0), explains its failure in characteristic p via the Artin–Schreier equation yᵖ − y = x⁻¹ and its root y = ∑ x^{−1/pᵏ}, lists what is proved, and an honesty note delimiting the negative (obstruction) result from the open positive analogue (Kedlaya / Artin–Schreier–Witt).
sections.mathContext: Sets up the contrast: char 0 ⟹ bounded ramification suffices (Puiseux); char p ⟹ Artin–Schreier wild ramification breaks boundedness.

sections.title: The Puiseux Predicate and Artin–Schreier Exponents
sections.summary: def IsPuiseuxSeries (verbatim from the gallery: ∃ n : ℕ+, every support exponent is k/n) and def artinSchreierExp p k = −1/p^{k+1}.
sections.mathContext: IsPuiseuxSeries encodes 'bounded ramification'; artinSchreierExp enumerates the exponents that violate it.

sections.title: Distinct Ramification Levels
sections.summary: artinSchreierExp_strictMono: the exponents are strictly increasing toward 0 (via antitonicity of 1/x and pow_lt_pow_right₀). artinSchreierExp_injective: hence pairwise distinct.
sections.mathContext: There are infinitely many distinct ramification levels −1/p, −1/p², −1/p³, …, so the obstruction is genuinely infinite, not a finite artifact.

sections.title: Unbounded Ramification (the Core)
sections.summary: artinSchreierExp_denominators_unbounded: no n : ℕ+ has every −1/p^{k+1} of the form j/n. Pick k with p^{k+1} > n; clearing denominators gives n = −j·p^{k+1}, so p^{k+1} ∣ n and p^{k+1} ≤ n — contradiction with the choice of k.
sections.mathContext: The single arithmetic fact behind the failure of Puiseux in characteristic p: the denominators pᵏ outrun any fixed common denominator n.

sections.title: The Artin–Schreier Obstruction
sections.summary: artinSchreier_support_not_puiseux: any Hahn series whose support contains all artinSchreierExp p k is not a Puiseux series — an immediate consequence of the unbounded-denominator core applied through the support.
sections.mathContext: Applied to the Artin–Schreier root y (support = {−1/pᵏ}), this is the formal statement that an algebraic element over the Laurent series fails to be Puiseux — Puiseux's theorem fails in characteristic p.

crossReferences.description: Parent: Puiseux's theorem in characteristic 0 (Puiseux series are the algebraic closure of the Laurent series). This entry answers its open question #1 on positive characteristic by formalizing the obstruction, reusing its IsPuiseuxSeries predicate.
Sibling open-question branch off the Puiseux theorem entry.

conclusion.summary: Machine-verified: the Artin–Schreier exponent set {−1/p^{k+1}} has unbounded ramification (lies in no (1/n)·ℤ), so any Hahn series carrying it — in particular the Artin–Schreier root of yᵖ − y = x⁻¹ — is not a Puiseux series. This is the precise, elementary obstruction showing Puiseux's theorem fails in positive characteristic. Zero sorries, zero axioms.
conclusion.implications: **Sharp negative answer**: classical Puiseux series can never be algebraically closed in characteristic p — the Artin–Schreier root is a concrete algebraic element they miss. **Division of labour for the open question**: the correct positive analogue (Kedlaya's automatic/additive Hahn series) must enlarge Puiseux series precisely to absorb unbounded-ramification elements like this one; this entry pins down what has to be added.
openQuestions: Construct the Artin–Schreier root y = ∑_{k≥1} x^{−1/pᵏ} as an actual HahnSeries ℚ (𝔽_p): prove its support {−1/pᵏ} is partially well-ordered (IsPWO) and that yᵖ − y = x⁻¹ via the Frobenius identity, making artinSchreier_support_not_puiseux non-vacuous internally rather than by appeal to the classical root.

Formalize Kedlaya's theorem: the algebraic closure of 𝔽_p((x)) is the field of 'automatic' (finite-state / additively generated) Hahn series — the correct positive-characteristic analogue of Puiseux's theorem, via Artin–Schreier–Witt theory.
Quantify the ramification growth under iterated Artin–Schreier extensions: the n-th tower has ramification denominators up to pⁿ, giving a concrete cofinal family of non-Puiseux algebraic elements.
Compare with the mixed-characteristic / Witt-vector analogue (perfectoid-style tilting), where similar unbounded-ramification phenomena are tamed by passing to perfections.
